clue.text: Run to fish — might play one?

parts.note: to run at the double is to go at speed, so run can mean double
the bass is a common sea and freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone dashing off to go fishing, with a hint that they might play something.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is an instrument that a musician might play, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician in an orchestra might well play this large stringed instrument.

parts.note: de is French for of
but introduces an objection, as in 'no buts'

explanation.surface: A foreign objection raised for the first time.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's first public showing on stage or in sport.

explanation.surface: An extremely talkative person and what they might do.
explanation.definitionFit: Farthest or greatest in degree; a talker would speak a great deal, read as two words.

clue.text: Part with a fan of the theatre

definitions.text: Part with a fan of the theatre

parts.words: Part with a fan of the theatre
parts.note: reads as a theatre lover's role, but means a stage character whose fan gives a play by Oscar Wilde its title

explanation.surface: A role played by someone who loves going to plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde's comedy is named after this heroine and her fan.

parts.note: reads as spotting sailors on a ship, but means churchmen of a diocese and pieces on a chessboard

explanation.surface: Spotting crew members aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior clergy each head a diocese, and chess has pieces of the same name.

clue.text: Mansion to let, possibly, in US

parts.note: a country seat is a large house

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of the word may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A large house up for rent, perhaps in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in Washington state, in the north-west of America.

explanation.surface: Noticing a tiny amount of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice something is to see it with the eye; a tiny dab or drop of liquid is also called this.

clue.text: Hoffmann's little boy has swallowed a bottle

indicators.note: has swallowed means the boy's name goes around the other letter

parts.note: Heinrich Hoffmann's Struwwelpeter has the tale of Fidgety Phil

explanation.surface: A child in a German storybook has swallowed a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: Heinrich Hoffmann's children's book Struwwelpeter includes 'Fidgety Philip', a boy who rocks on his chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A small glass vessel for medicine or perfume.

parts.note: reads as ..., but means what is used for the sick: medical care

explanation.surface: Being treated badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical care given to patients; also the way someone is handled.

parts.note: reads as the commonest tool, but the main is the sea and the screw is a ship's propeller, driven by a rotating rod

explanation.surface: The commonest kind of screwdriver in a toolbox.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating rod from a ship's engine that turns the screw at the stern.

indicators.note: wrongly suggests the letters of the words are put in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something just happens to have been placed in the wrong spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' reads as one phrase, but 'to' belongs with the definition; 'wrongly' rearranges BE SITED.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned verb meaning befalls, as in 'woe betide him'.

explanation.surface: A way of travelling that underwater divers might use.
explanation.definitionFit: A company flying passengers is a carrier of this kind; a deep-sea diver's breathing tube is also an air line.

indicators.note: bungled tells us the letters of the two words are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Teachers who made a mess of things being dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: To discard or dismiss something is to get rid of it, as a court dismisses a case.

indicators.note: about means the word for land goes around the other piece

parts.note: a plot is a small piece of ground
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: An aviator coming down to earth near a single spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The person flying an aircraft is its captain at the controls.

parts.note: corn is a general word for cereal grain

explanation.surface: A breakfast bowl of cereal served in a cup instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The nut of the oak sits in a small scaly cup, and it is a grain-like seed, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: A doctor caused trouble — hold up results from this

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: trouble means the letters of the word are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor causes problems, and a delay follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges CAUSED to USCADE; the definition is an attack from hiding, from which a hold-up follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for an ambush, a surprise attack by people lying in wait.

parts.note: reads as low spirits after an attack, but means a crater in the ground left by an exploding artillery round

explanation.surface: Feeling low after being under fire in a war.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater blasted in the ground by an exploding shell is a hollow left after artillery fire.

parts.note: reads as RAF personnel, but means men who play airs (tunes) in church services

explanation.surface: Pilots serving in the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Church musicians play the keyboard instrument at worship.

clue.text: A bloomer, giving trophy for something churned out?

indicators.note: trophy comes after the churned product, in the order the answer needs

parts.note: butter is made by churning cream
a cup is a trophy given to a winner

explanation.surface: A blunder in awarding a prize for mass-produced goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bloomer' suggests a mistake but means a flower, a common yellow meadow plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything that flowers can be called a bloomer, and this is a yellow wild flower.

clue.text: British short-story writer — eccentric about pop pieces

indicators.note: about means the eccentric goes around the broken word

parts.note: a card is an odd or amusing person

indicators.note: in pieces means the word is broken up and its letters reordered

explanation.surface: A writer who is odd about pop music in bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' breaks POP into OPP, which goes inside CARD. A. E. Coppard was an English writer of short stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A. E. Coppard was an English author famed for his short fiction.

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
able means capable or skilled

explanation.surface: A Bible story set as the standard for skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A short moral tale such as those Jesus told in the Gospels.

indicators.note: some say tells us a word is said aloud and sounds like the answer

parts.note: consumed food means ate it

explanation.surface: How many were eaten, according to some people.
explanation.definitionFit: A number between seven and nine.

clue.text: Climb was ruined by Mr Turner

indicators.note: by places one piece beside the other
ruined means the three letters of the word are wrecked and reassembled
a turner is something that turns, here turning the title round

parts.note: Mr is taken as its own two letters

explanation.surface: A climb spoilt by the painter Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mr Turner' looks like the painter, but 'Turner' turns MR round to RM, after SWA from 'was ruined'.
explanation.definitionFit: To shin up a pole or rope is to climb it this way.

indicators.note: repair suggests the letters are taken apart and put back together differently

explanation.surface: Fixing blame for a slow walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely walking speed, a gentle stroll.

parts.note: reads as music practised for a stage show, but means songs written for several singing parts, as roles are learned

explanation.surface: Music someone has learned for an opera performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral pieces for several voices each singing a separate line.

explanation.surface: An artist who is tidy and straightforward.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Wilson Steer was an English painter; neat is an old word for cattle, here a young bullock; and to direct is to guide.

clue.text: Late bar members resettle in Canada

indicators.note: the members, here the letters of the words, settle again in a new order

explanation.surface: Barristers arriving late move house to Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar members' suggests lawyers, but 'members resettle' rearranges LATE BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie province of western Canada.

clue.text: Effrontery that is needed to join an old golf-club

parts.note: brass, as in brass neck, means cheek or impudence

explanation.surface: Someone needs nerve to get into an old golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golf-club' suggests a society, but it is the stick: an old wooden club roughly like a modern two-wood.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsolete wooden golf stick with a brass sole, used for long shots.

explanation.surface: There is still time to write some verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Still can mean yet more, as in 'even better'; evening is called this in poetic language.

clue.text: No doubt he hopes his writing will sell

definitions.text: No doubt he hopes his writing will sell

parts.words: No doubt he hopes his writing will sell
parts.note: reads as an author hoping for sales, but means someone who puts notices in the paper to sell goods

explanation.surface: An author hoping their book becomes a bestseller.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone placing a notice in a newspaper wants buyers for whatever is offered.
